Adventure Tyres: Finding the Right Balance

Adventure bike tyres must compromise between on-road grip and off-road traction. The perfect balance depends entirely on your riding — a rider who spends 90 percent of their time on tarmac needs very different rubber than someone exploring green lanes every weekend. Understanding the tyre spectrum helps you make the right choice.

The Adventure Tyre Spectrum

  • 90/10 road-biased — Essentially touring tyres with a slightly more aggressive tread pattern. Excellent on-road grip and longevity with enough tread to handle dry gravel tracks. Ideal for riders who rarely leave tarmac.
  • 70/30 road-biased — The most popular choice for UK adventure riders. Meaningful tread blocks provide genuine off-road grip on green lanes while maintaining confident on-road performance. The sweet spot for mixed touring.
  • 50/50 dual-purpose — Equal emphasis on road and trail. Noticeable tread noise on tarmac and slightly reduced corner grip compared to road-biased options, but genuine off-road capability on mud, sand, and gravel.
  • 80/20 trail-biased — Aggressive tread pattern for serious off-road use. Compromised on-road grip and rapid wear on tarmac. Only for riders spending the majority of their time off-road.

Best Adventure Tyres 2026

Michelin Anakee Adventure (70/30) — The default choice for UK adventure riders. Excellent wet road grip, reasonable off-road capability on dry trails, and good longevity. A safe and competent all-rounder.

Continental TKC 70 Rocks (60/40) — More aggressive than the Michelin with better off-road grip while maintaining acceptable road performance. The Rocks compound is optimised for UK conditions.

Bridgestone AX41 (50/50) — A genuine 50/50 tyre with impressive off-road grip and surprisingly acceptable road manners. The best choice for riders who regularly tackle challenging trails.

Mitas E-07+ (60/40) — Outstanding value with good off-road performance and reasonable road grip. The plus compound improves wet-road performance over the original E-07.

For most UK adventure riders, a 70/30 road-biased tyre is the sweet spot. Our green lanes and byways rarely require aggressive off-road rubber, and you spend far more time on tarmac where road grip matters most for safety.

Tyre Pressure for Mixed Riding

Run road pressures on tarmac and reduce by 0.3-0.5 bar for extended off-road sections to improve grip and comfort. Always reinflate to road pressures before returning to tarmac, as low-pressure cornering on paved roads is dangerous and accelerates tyre wear dramatically.

Running In New Adventure Tyres

New adventure tyres have a shiny release agent on the surface that dramatically reduces grip until worn off. Spend the first fifty to one hundred miles riding gently, progressively leaning further with each bend as the surface scrubs in. Never fit new tyres the day before a tour — run them in during the preceding week to ensure full confidence from mile one of your adventure. Adjustable pressures adapt the same tyre to mixed terrain.
